subject: Astronomy & Space
title: The Solar Wind
description: A 60-second lesson on The Solar Wind.

hook.text: The Sun constantly blows a stream of charged particles outward at 400–800 km/s. This solar wind fills the solar system.

buildup.text: It's mostly protons and electrons from the Sun's corona. The wind carries the Sun's magnetic field outward with it.

discovery.text: Eugene Parker predicted the solar wind in 1958. Many doubted him, but spacecraft quickly confirmed his theory.

twist.text: The solar wind creates the heliosphere—a protective bubble around the solar system that deflects most galactic cosmic rays.

climax.text: Parker Solar Probe is flying through the corona itself—touching the Sun at just 6 million km from its surface.

punchline.text: A constant wind of particles from the Sun. It shields our entire solar system.

quiz.question: What is the heliosphere?
options: A protective bubble created by the solar wind that shields the solar system from galactic cosmic rays
The visible atmosphere of the Sun seen during solar eclipses
A region near the Sun where temperatures exceed one million degrees

details.summary: The solar wind is a continuous stream of charged particles (mostly protons and electrons) flowing outward from the Sun's corona at 300-800 km/s. It carries the Sun's magnetic field throughout the solar system, shapes planetary magnetospheres, creates comet tails, and defines the boundary of the…
details.whyItMatters: The solar wind creates the space environment that all solar system bodies exist within. It shapes magnetospheres, drives atmospheric loss on unprotected planets, and defines the Sun's sphere of influence.
takeaways: Continuous stream of charged particles from the Sun's corona
Flows at 300-800 km/s carrying the Sun's magnetic field
Shapes planetary magnetospheres and creates comet tails

faq.question: Does the solar wind affect Earth directly?
faq.answer: Earth's magnetic field deflects most solar wind particles, but some funnel along field lines toward the poles, creating auroras. During strong solar wind events, the magnetosphere compresses and geomagnetic storms can affect satellites, GPS, and power grids.

faq.question: Where does the solar wind end?
faq.answer: At the heliopause, about 120 astronomical units from the Sun, where solar wind pressure balances the interstellar medium. Voyager 1 crossed this boundary in 2012, becoming the first human-made object in interstellar space. The solar wind's influence creates a bubble called the heliosphere.
